articles.title: Following OpenAI, Anthropic is also reportedly postponing its IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic is reportedly delaying its IPO from October to November 2026 to present strong Q3 results. Investors expect a roughly $2 trillion valuation, but rising infrastructure costs, including $1.25 billion a month for its SpaceX deal alone, and unresolved security risks complicate the listing. The article Following OpenAI, Anthropic is also reportedly postponing its IPO appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: Investing for the AI Boom: Masters in Business with Glen Kacher
articles.summary: Barry speaks with Glen Kacher, Managing Director and CIO of Light Street Capital. They discuss his tenure at Integral Capital Partners, as well as his start at Tiger Management under founder Julian Robertson. They discuss being a hedge fund surrounded by venture capital in Silicon Valley, as well as learning to embrace the speed of tech. They also discuss the polarization of data centers and what AI will look like five years from now. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nvidia-Backed Data Center Firm Nscale Files Publicly for IPO
articles.summary: Nscale, a developer of artificial intelligence data centers that counts Nvidia Corp. and Microsoft Corp. among its partners, filed for an initial public offering in New York to fund the equipment satisfying AI’s insatiable demand for computing power.

articles.title: AI Boom Risks a ‘Corporate Extinction Event’: Paul
articles.summary: Sherry Paul, managing director and private wealth advisor at Morgan Stanley, says companies that fail to embrace AI risk being overtaken by competitors that use the technology to boost productivity and profitability. “We move into what I call the corporate extinction event,” Paul says on “Bloomberg Surveillance,” comparing the disruption to Netflix overtaking Blockbuster. This interview aired Sept. 17, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 💻 A Full-Fledged Trading Engine for the Node.js Ecosystem
articles.summary: You can check out the project repo here Over the past five years the Node.js ecosystem has stabilized. Nothing fundamentally new shows up in it: we discuss why Fastify beats Express, choose between Prisma and Drizzle, argue about ESM versus CommonJS, and swap one bundler for another that does the same thing, only faster. The niches are taken, the tools are mature, the hype has moved to neighboring runtimes. That is good news for production and boring news for an engineer. Which makes it all the more interesting when an entire new application domain opens up in the ecosystem. Backtest as one of the execution modes The library is a toolkit for algorithmic trading that extends Node.js into territory historically ruled by Python alone: Backtrader, VectorBT, Freqtrade. The very same trading strategy runs in both live and backtest without changes backtest-kit dashboard The difference is fundamental. articles.title: AI/ML and sensitive production data in fintech and healthcare? Where is the data going? Can it be made sense of? [D]
articles.summary: Hi all! i am currently working as a software engineer for a pretty big enterprise fintech company here in the states. In the the last 12 months at my job there has been a huge push for developers to use ai and agentic program in our development cycle, first in our ide directly, then Coder space instances with cloud agents and now code vulnerability remediation. This has gotten me thinking beyond developer productivity and more about how ML/AI systems can actually be integrated into production environments in highly regulated industries like fintech and healthcare. This makes me think "But hmmm... with a direct connection to sensitive production data, how do you design the architecture so that sensitive financial data doesn’t unnecessarily leave your environment?
